title: How to Get By in India When You Have No Money
intro: Chapter 7: How to Get By in India When You Have No Money. The routes that actually exist here - ration cards, pensions, legal aid, labour offices, night shelters - and the ones that do not, with the official source for each.

tips.title: India has no national unemployment insurance - check ESIC's unemployment allowance, EPFO and MGNREGA instead
tips.cost: No fee. You need Aadhaar, a bank account in your own name, your UAN or ESIC insurance number, and the date your job ended. Most of it is online: the ESIC portal, the EPFO member portal, or your state employment exchange. The hard part is that no single office pays an unemployment cheque, so you may have to ask two or three before you find the route that fits you.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not run a national unemployment insurance fund that pays a monthly benefit after redundancy. The cover is a patchwork. ESIC's Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana pays a cash allowance to insured workers who lose employment, if they meet ESIC's contribution and claim conditions. EPFO returns your own provident fund and, below ten years of service, a withdrawal benefit instead of a pension. MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage work a year to rural households. State labour welfare boards add their own relief. Apply to each separately. None of them replaces a salary, and there is no fixed 12, 18 or 24 month ladder.
tips.benefit: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana is the closest Indian scheme to an unemployment benefit: a time-limited cash allowance for insured persons who lose employment, with the rate, duration and conditions set by ESIC and published on its site. EPFO pays out your accumulated provident fund after two months of unemployment, and a withdrawal benefit if your pensionable service is under ten years; at ten years or more you keep a monthly EPS pension instead. MGNREGA gives every rural household at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year; section 7(1) requires a daily unemployment allowance if work is not provided within fifteen days of a valid application. Building and construction workers' boards, funded by the BOCW cess, pay injury, death and some distress benefits to registered workers.
tips.sources: Employees' State Insurance Corporation - Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and the EPF Scheme, 1952, paragraph 69. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, sections 3 and 7. <https://nrega.nic.in/>; Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 1996. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no direct Indian equivalent of a contributory unemployment insurance fund with statutory benefit durations. ABVKY is conditional and time-limited, and ESIC decides when claims are open, so check the current circular before you rely on it. An early PF withdrawal cuts your retirement corpus. MGNREGA is for rural households and pays the notified wage rate for manual work, not a salary. State schemes change with governments; confirm with the state labour department, never with a paid agent.

tips.title: An unpaid-wage complaint goes to the labour commissioner first; labour court and arbitration come after, and neither charges a court fee
tips.cost: No court fee, and no lawyer is required at the first stage. You need the appointment letter, salary slips, bank statements, attendance or shift records, and the WhatsApp or email trail. Budget one to three visits to the labour office, or file online through SAMADHAN. The delay, not the fee, is the real cost.
tips.inPlainWords: India routes wage claims through the labour administration, not straight to a court. File a complaint with the state Labour Commissioner office, or with the Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) if your employer is in the central sphere, such as banks, mines, ports and central public sector units. Under the Code on Wages, 2019, a claims authority can hear wage claims; conciliation is free under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, and the dispute can go to a labour court or tribunal. The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 are repealed. The limitation period differs, so confirm it before filing.
tips.benefit: Three free doors. First, the labour commissioner inspection and conciliation machinery. Second, the claims authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, which can order payment of deducted or delayed wages and compensation. Third, reference to a labour court or industrial tribunal under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, whose award is enforceable as a decree. The four labour codes commenced on 21 November 2025, with savings for pending cases. SAMADHAN (samadhan.labour.gov.in) accepts industrial-dispute filings online.
tips.sources: Code on Wages, 2019. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Industrial Relations Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Ministry of Labour and Employment commencement notifications, 21 November 2025. <https://labour.gov.in/>; SAMADHAN portal. <https://samadhan.labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Coverage decides everything: managerial and supervisory staff may fall outside the Industrial Relations Code definition of workman, and small establishments may be outside the state Shops Act. The limitation period differs, so confirm it before you file. A win is not a payment: if the employer has no assets, enforcement is slow. Free legal aid is covered in tip 7-3.

tips.title: Free legal aid covers wage claims, maintenance and work injury - call 15100 or the district legal services authority
tips.cost: Nothing. Legal aid is free to the person who receives it, including the lawyer's fee, and eligible cases get court-fee exemption. You need proof of the category you fall under and a short written account of the dispute.
tips.inPlainWords: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 gives free legal aid to listed categories: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, women, children, persons with disabilities, industrial workmen, persons in custody, victims of trafficking, disaster or ethnic violence, and anyone whose annual income is below the limit the state government sets. Apply at the District Legal Services Authority in the district court complex, at the State Legal Services Authority, or through the NALSA helpline 15100. Lok Adalats settle many wage and maintenance disputes at no cost. There is no fee to apply and no need for a ration card.
tips.benefit: Section 12 of the Act lists the eligible categories, and section 13 provides free legal services, which include a lawyer, drafting and court-fee exemption. Section 12(f) covers industrial workmen, which is the route for most wage and retrenchment disputes, and section 12(g) covers a person in custody or a person in a protective home. Section 12(h) covers anyone whose income is below the state-notified ceiling, so a salaried worker made redundant can qualify. Lok Adalats under section 19 can settle a dispute, and their award is final and binding with no appeal. NALSA also runs legal aid clinics in prisons, juvenile homes and shelter homes.
tips.sources: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, sections 12, 13 and 19. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority - legal aid. <https://nalsa.gov.in/legal-aid/>; Department of Justice - legal aid and the 15100 helpline. <https://doj.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Eligibility is not automatic for everyone: income ceilings are set by each state and change. Legal aid lawyers vary in quality and caseload, and you can ask the authority for a different panel lawyer if yours does nothing for weeks. Legal aid does not cover a private-lawyer fee you have already agreed to pay. There is no Indian rule that removes the need to show hardship: you still have to show you fall in a listed category.

tips.title: India has no statutory 10-day shelter with a travel voucher - municipal night shelters are the closest route
tips.cost: Usually free. Urban night shelters, called rain baseras, run by municipal corporations under the urban shelter programme take walk-ins, and state welfare homes and NGO shelters take referrals. You may be asked for a name and sometimes an ID. The hard part is finding a bed: capacity is small and it is first come, first served.
tips.inPlainWords: There is no Indian statute that guarantees a homeless person ten days of food and lodging plus a ticket home. What exists is a municipal patchwork. Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission, urban local bodies are funded to run shelters for the urban homeless, usually called rain baseras, with beds, water and toilets. State social welfare departments run similar homes, and NGOs run others. For women in distress there are One Stop Centres and the 181 helpline; for children, 1098. Nobody hands out cash at the door. If you are on the street at night, call 112.
tips.benefit: The DAY-NULM shelter component funds urban local bodies to provide shelter with beds, drinking water, sanitation and basic security, and many states publish shelter lists. One Stop Centres under the Ministry of Women and Child Development give temporary shelter, medical aid and legal help to women facing violence. Childline 1098 responds to children living on the street. State-run destitute homes and beggars' homes exist in most states under social welfare departments. None of these issues a travel voucher, and none has a statutory maximum stay you can enforce.
tips.sources: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs - DAY-NULM, Shelter for Urban Homeless. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development - One Stop Centres. <https://wcd.nic.in/>; Emergency Response Support System - 112. <https://112.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This tip has no direct Indian equivalent, and the difference matters: no statute obliges any Indian shelter to admit you for ten days, and no government office issues a free ticket home as a matter of right. Shelter capacity is far below need in most cities, and many rain baseras close or run at reduced capacity outside winter. Police can move people off pavements. Carry ID if you have it, keep your belongings with you, and treat any private home that demands money or documents with suspicion.

tips.title: Use the free National Career Service and state employment exchanges before paying any placement agency
tips.cost: No fee. Register on ncs.gov.in with Aadhaar or a mobile number, upload a CV, and use the job fairs and career counselling. State employment exchanges register you for free. The time cost is a few hours, plus travel to a job fair.
tips.inPlainWords: The National Career Service is the central government's free job-matching platform: vacancies, job fairs, career counselling, skilling links and registration with state employment exchanges. Registration is free and employers are checked before posting. State employment exchanges still maintain live registers for some government and private vacancies. e-Shram registers unorganised workers and gives you a universal account number. None of this guarantees a job. What it does is put you in front of employers without paying a commission, which matters when cash is short.
tips.benefit: NCS offers free registration, job search, alerts, career counselling and a network of model career centres, and it links to skilling programmes. State employment exchanges issue registration certificates that some public-sector and state government recruitments still ask for. e-Shram gives unorganised workers a UAN and an entry point to several social-security schemes. Because these are public services they cannot charge a placement fee, unlike private consultancies that often ask for a month's salary.
tips.sources: National Career Service, Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://www.ncs.gov.in/>; e-Shram, Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://eshram.gov.in/>; Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: NCS listings are uneven by state and sector, and many blue-collar jobs never appear there. Employment exchange registration is close to vestigial for private jobs in many states. Never pay a registration or interview fee to a private agency; see tip 7-15. For daily-wage work, verify the rate on site and keep the contractor's name and phone number.

tips.title: There is no national emergency cash grant for sudden hardship - the district collector and the CM Relief Fund are the closest routes
tips.cost: No fee. You write an application to the tehsildar, block development officer or district collector, attach proof of the event such as a fire report, hospital discharge summary, death certificate or post-mortem report, and follow up in person. Expect two to four visits.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not have a nationwide emergency assistance payment for a household hit by fire, accident or sudden illness, of the kind any resident can claim as a right. The nearest routes are discretionary. The district administration can sanction relief from the State Disaster Response Fund, but the SDRF norms are written for notified natural calamities and cover house damage, injury and death, not ordinary medical bills. Chief Minister's Relief Funds accept applications for medical treatment and distress. Some states run their own distress funds. Approval is discretionary and slow, so treat it as a supplement, not a plan.
tips.benefit: State Disaster Response Fund norms laid down by the Ministry of Home Affairs provide gratuitous relief and compensation for loss of life, injury and house damage after notified disasters, and district collectors can sanction immediate relief. Chief Minister's Relief Funds are not constituted under the Disaster Management Act, 2005: section 46 of that Act constitutes only the National Disaster Response Fund, and the state and district funds are provided for elsewhere in the Act. A CMRF is a discretionary fund set up by each state government's own order or rules, which is why the sums, the eligibility and the paperwork differ from state to state. PM-JAY and state health schemes cover hospital costs, which is usually the larger bill; see tip 7-10. For a death in the family, the National Family Benefit Scheme under NSAP pays a lump sum to a BPL household that loses its primary earner.
tips.sources: Ministry of Home Affairs - State Disaster Response Fund norms. <https://mha.gov.in/>; National Disaster Management Authority. <https://ndma.gov.in/>; National Social Assistance Programme - National Family Benefit Scheme. <https://nsap.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: This is not an entitlement you can enforce. SDRF relief is tied to notified disasters, and a house fire or a road accident may not qualify in your district. CM Relief Fund decisions are discretionary, with no appeal. Never pay a middleman who promises to get you relief; applications are free.

tips.title: If household income is below the state line, the ration card under the National Food Security Act is the real safety net
tips.cost: No fee for a ration card in most states, though some charge a nominal application fee. You apply at the block or tehsil food and civil supplies office, or online through the state PDS portal, with Aadhaar, address proof and income information. Expect two or three visits and a verification round.
tips.inPlainWords: India's income-tested food scheme is the National Food Security Act, 2013, not a cash benefit. Eligible households get 5 kg of grain per person per month as priority households, or 35 kg per household per month as Antyodaya Anna Yojana households. The Act's coverage is capped at 75 per cent of the rural population and 50 per cent of the urban population, and each state decides who is included. Entitlement is in kind, through the fair price shop, at a price fixed by the Centre. One Nation One Ration Card lets a migrant draw the entitlement at any fair price shop after eKYC.
tips.benefit: Section 3 of the Act creates the grain entitlement, 5 kg per person per month for priority households and 35 kg per household per month for Antyodaya households, and section 4 covers women and children, including a maternity benefit of not less than Rs 6,000. ONORC makes the card portable across states after eKYC, so a migrant can draw grain where they work. Where grain is not supplied, the Act provides for a food security allowance. Antyodaya and priority status also unlock other state benefits, from free school meals to some health top-ups.
tips.sources: National Food Security Act, 2013. <https://nfsa.gov.in/>; Department of Food and Public Distribution - ONORC. <https://dfpd.gov.in/>; National Food Security Act text. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no direct Indian equivalent of a monthly cash payment set at the poverty line. NFSA gives grain, not money, and the quantity is small. Inclusion is decided by state surveys and the list is often frozen, so a newly poor household may be refused a new card. Ration cards are also a known source of leakage and exclusion; check your name on the state PDS portal. Antyodaya cards are capped, so eligibility does not guarantee one.

tips.title: Get a UDID card first, then claim the disability pension and any state caregiver allowance
tips.cost: No fee for the UDID card application in most states. You need a disability certificate from a government hospital or medical board, identity proof and a photograph. The assessment can take weeks, and travel to the medical board is the real cost.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no single pair of living and care subsidies issued together. The structure is different. Get a Unique Disability ID card from the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities; it records your disability percentage and is the key to most benefits. Then apply for the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension under NSAP, a small monthly central pension for people with severe or multiple disabilities aged 18 to 79, and for whatever disability pension your state pays on top. Some states also pay a caregiver allowance, run day-care centres and give assistive devices under the ADIP scheme.
tips.benefit: The UDID card is a single document accepted across central and state schemes. NSAP's Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme pays a central pension to persons with severe or multiple disabilities in BPL households, and states usually add a top-up; the current central rates are published by NSAP and revised from time to time. The ADIP scheme supplies assistive devices at subsidised cost. State disability pensions, caregiver allowances and travel concessions vary widely, so check your state disability welfare department. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 adds reservation in government jobs and education.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities - UDID. <https://www.swavlambancard.gov.in/>; National Social Assistance Programme. <https://nsap.nic.in/>; Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; ADIP scheme. <https://depwd.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This is not the same as a two-tier living and care subsidy. The central disability pension is small and is meant to be topped up by the state; the total may still be a few hundred rupees a month. A UDID card needs a medical assessment, and the percentage recorded decides eligibility. If you cannot apply in person, a family member can file on your behalf with a written authorisation.

tips.title: Check whether PM-JAY or ESIC already covers you before paying any private health premium
tips.cost: Free if you are eligible for PM-JAY or ESIC. PM-JAY has no annual individual premium. ESIC is contributory: 0.75 per cent of wages from the employee and 3.25 per cent from the employer in covered establishments. A private family floater is the only route that costs you a real annual premium, typically several thousand rupees.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not charge an annual individual premium for its flagship public scheme. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY gives eligible families Rs 5 lakh of cashless secondary and tertiary hospital cover per year, with no cap on family size or age, at empanelled hospitals. Eligibility comes from the SECC 2011 deprivation criteria and occupational categories, and since 2024 everyone aged 70 and above is covered regardless of income through the Ayushman Vay Vandana card. ESIC covers employees of registered establishments and their families. State schemes such as Aarogyasri add cover in some states. Check your eligibility on the PM-JAY portal before buying anything.
tips.benefit: PM-JAY pays up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation, including most pre-existing conditions from day one, with no waiting period and no exclusion for age. The Ayushman card is issued after eKYC at a Common Service Centre, an empanelled hospital or online. ESIC gives insured workers and dependants free medical care plus cash benefits for sickness, maternity and employment injury. If you are covered by either, a private policy is a top-up, not a necessity; see tip 7-20. Hospital empanelment matters more than the sum insured, so check that your district hospital is on the list.
tips.sources: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/PM-JAY>; PM-JAY senior citizens 70+ FAQ. <https://nha.gov.in/img/resources/English_FAQs_related_to_the_benefits_for_senior_citizens.pdf>; Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no Indian equivalent of an annual enrolment window with a waiting-period penalty for missing it. PM-JAY eligibility is fixed by central and state lists, and being poor does not automatically put you on them. Many private hospitals are not empanelled. ESIC coverage ends when insurable employment ends. State schemes differ sharply, so check the state health agency, not a hospital's billing desk.

tips.title: For a serious illness, work the public ladder in order: PM-JAY or ESIC, then the state scheme, then hospital charity - not an instant loan app
tips.cost: No fee to apply. The costs are travel, paperwork and time: eKYC for the Ayushman card, pre-authorisation at the hospital, and a state scheme application if you are outside PM-JAY. Keep every discharge summary, bill and investigation report.
tips.inPlainWords: The sequence matters. First confirm your public cover, PM-JAY, ESIC or a state scheme, and get the Ayushman card or ESIC referral before admission if you can. Second, use an empanelled hospital so the bill is cashless; a non-empanelled hospital means paying first and claiming later, which most schemes do not allow. Third, if a bill still lands on you, apply to the hospital's poor-patient fund, the Chief Minister's Relief Fund and the Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi for treatment in central government hospitals. Fourth, if you are insured under ESIC, claim sickness benefit for the days you cannot work. Do not take an instant loan app loan while a public scheme is pending.
tips.benefit: PM-JAY's Rs 5 lakh cover is cashless at empanelled hospitals and includes pre-existing disease from day one. ESIC pays sickness benefit for up to 91 days in a year at a wage-linked rate, extended in longer illnesses, plus full medical care for the insured person and dependants. Employment injury is now governed by Chapter VII of the Social Security Code, 2020, which replaced the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923; ESIC administers it and pays disablement benefit and dependants' pension. The Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi funds treatment of BPL patients in central government hospitals, and state CM Relief Funds accept medical applications. Ask the hospital's medical social worker: most large government hospitals have one, and they know which fund is open.
tips.sources: National Health Authority - PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/PM-JAY>; ESIC - sickness and employment injury benefits. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Social Security Code, 2020 (Chapter VII, employment injury benefit). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare - Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no Indian equivalent of a statutory medical-leave ladder of 3 to 24 months that protects your job. ESIC sickness benefit is time-limited and only for insured workers; outside ESIC, paid sick leave depends on your contract or the state Shops Act. PM-JAY does not cover outpatient care, medicines or diagnostics, which is where most of a poor household's health spending goes. Cashless admission can be refused if pre-authorisation is not done, so start the paperwork before the surgery, not after.

tips.title: A lost Aadhaar can be downloaded again in minutes; there is no temporary Aadhaar, so carry a second photo ID
tips.cost: Downloading e-Aadhaar is free; a reprint at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra costs a small fee. A duplicate voter ID, PAN reprint or driving licence reprint carries a small statutory fee. A police complaint for lost documents is free.
tips.inPlainWords: Aadhaar is not reissued as a physical card on demand, and there is no temporary Aadhaar. What you do is download the e-Aadhaar PDF from the UIDAI site using your Aadhaar number and an OTP, then print it; it is a valid copy. For a lost PAN, apply for a reprint through NSDL or UTIITSL. For a voter ID, download the e-EPIC from the Election Commission. For a driving licence, apply for a duplicate on Parivahan. DigiLocker holds digital copies of many of these. File a police lost-document report so misuse can be traced, and keep the acknowledgement.
tips.benefit: e-Aadhaar is legally equivalent to the printed card and carries a digital signature. UIDAI's resident portal also lets you retrieve your Aadhaar number if you have forgotten it. The Election Commission's voters' portal issues e-EPIC, and Parivahan issues duplicate licences and registration certificates. DigiLocker, run by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, stores issuer-signed copies that many offices accept. A police lost-report is the document that protects you if someone uses your identity for a loan or a SIM.
tips.sources: Unique Identification Authority of India - e-Aadhaar and Aadhaar retrieval. <https://uidai.gov.in/>; Election Commission of India - e-EPIC. <https://voters.eci.gov.in/>; Parivahan Sewa, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://parivahan.gov.in/>; DigiLocker. <https://www.digilocker.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no Indian rule that a replacement ID must be issued within 60 days, and no three-day temporary card. Aadhaar is not mandatory for every service, and the Supreme Court in 2018 struck down several linkage requirements, but many offices still ask for it, so carry a second ID. Never give your Aadhaar OTP or biometrics to an agent who offers to update your card for a fee.

tips.title: Employment exchange registration is free but thin - the working routes are NCS, e-Shram and state welfare board membership
tips.cost: No fee. Registration on NCS and e-Shram is online and free; state employment exchange registration is free at the counter. The time cost is gathering the certificates, such as caste, income, disability and BPL documents, that decide which schemes you can use.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no person facing employment difficulties certificate with the bundle of subsidies that name implies elsewhere. Registration with a state employment exchange creates a live-register entry that some government recruitments still require, and NCS gives you job alerts. e-Shram registers unorganised workers and issues a UAN that is now the entry point for several social-security schemes. For targeted help the practical documents are the BPL or Antyodaya ration card, the UDID for disability, and the SC, ST or OBC certificate. Each unlocks a different set of schemes, and none of them pays a wage.
tips.benefit: e-Shram registration is free, gives a universal account number, and is used to channel schemes for gig, construction and domestic workers. State welfare boards, such as construction workers' boards under the BOCW Act and, in some states, domestic workers' and gig workers' boards, charge a small registration fee and pay injury, maternity and sometimes pension benefits. NCS lists job fairs and skilling courses. Apprenticeship under NAPS pays a stipend with government support; see tip 7-13. Employment exchange registration remains a documentary requirement for a few state government posts.
tips.sources: National Career Service. <https://www.ncs.gov.in/>; e-Shram. <https://eshram.gov.in/>; Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 1996 and state welfare boards. <https://labour.gov.in/>; Code on Social Security, 2020 - gig and platform workers. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This tip has no direct Indian equivalent: there is no recognition that triggers a social-insurance subsidy for an unemployed self-employed person. State welfare board benefits require you to be registered before the event, so join while you are working. Registration alone creates no entitlement to a job. Beware of agents charging for e-Shram or NCS registration, which is free.

tips.title: Skill training under PMKVY and apprenticeships under NAPS are free or stipend-paid - do not pay a private institute first
tips.cost: PMKVY short-term courses are free and include assessment and certification. Apprenticeships pay you a stipend, of which the government reimburses part to the employer. The real cost is the hours and the travel to the training centre.
tips.inPlainWords: India subsidises training by paying providers, not by reimbursing you, so the usual route is a free course rather than a refund. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana runs short-term courses through empanelled training partners, with free assessment and certification. Skill India Digital lists courses and their eligibility. National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme apprenticeships combine on-the-job training with a stipend, and the government shares the stipend cost with the employer. ITIs, Jan Shikshan Sansthan centres and PM-DAKSH cover different groups. Check the provider is empanelled before you sign anything.
tips.benefit: PMKVY covers short-term skilling, recognition of prior learning and upskilling, with the cost borne by the scheme for eligible candidates. NAPS reimburses 25 per cent of the prescribed stipend, up to Rs 1,500 per month per apprentice, to the employer, which is why employers take apprentices. PM-DAKSH pays for training of SC, ST, OBC, EWS, women and transgender candidates. Jan Shikshan Sansthan focuses on adults with low literacy. Skill India Digital issues verifiable certificates that some employers now check digitally.
tips.sources: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana - Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. <https://www.pmkvyofficial.org/>; Skill India Digital. <https://www.skillindiadigital.gov.in/>; National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme. <https://www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in/>; PM-DAKSH. <https://pmdaksh.dosje.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no Indian scheme that reimburses you for a course you chose and paid for. PMKVY quality varies enormously by training partner, so ask for the placement record and the assessment body before enrolling. A guaranteed job promise is a warning sign. Apprenticeship stipends are low, a prescribed share of the minimum wage, and not every apprentice is retained.

tips.title: Job hunting is a skill, not a volume game: coaching, clear goals and asking for referrals roughly double the odds
tips.cost: No money. It takes one to two hours a day for several weeks. Free career counselling is available through NCS model career centres and district employment exchanges; paid coaching is optional.
tips.inPlainWords: A meta-analysis of 47 controlled studies found that people who went through structured job-search coaching were about 2.67 times more likely to find work than those who did not. The parts that did the work were concrete search skills, practice in presenting yourself, specific goals, proactive action and asking other people for help. The last one is the one people skip. In India the free version of this is NCS career counselling plus a written plan: which roles, which employers, how many applications a week, and who you will ask for a referral.
tips.benefit: The effect size comes from Liu, Huang and Wang (2014), a meta-analysis of 47 experimental and quasi-experimental studies, with an odds ratio of 2.67 for employment. Programmes that combined skill-building with motivation and social support performed best. The Indian implementation is unglamorous: register on NCS, attend a job fair, keep your documents in one folder, write a one-page CV, and ask five people a week for an introduction. Public career counselling at model career centres is free.
tips.sources: Liu S, Huang JL, Wang M (2014). Effectiveness of job search interventions: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin 140(4): 1009-1041. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0035923>; National Career Service - career counselling and job fairs. <https://www.ncs.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The 47 studies were mostly run in Europe and North America; none of them tested Indian labour markets, so the 2.67 figure is an extrapolation, not an Indian result. Coaching improves your odds, it does not create vacancies. Referrals work best where you already have a network; if you do not, job fairs and NCS listings are the substitute.

tips.title: No deposit, no original documents, no training loan, no chain scheme, no moneylender without a licence
tips.cost: Zero. Say no at the counter and keep the chat log, the receipt and the advertisement. If you have already paid, a written complaint to the labour commissioner and a police complaint for cheating cost nothing.
tips.inPlainWords: Five rules. An employer may not keep your original certificates as security, and a wage deduction is lawful only if it falls in the permitted categories under the Code on Wages, 2019; a deposit or training fee usually does not. A recruitment agency that charges you for a placement is a warning sign, and for overseas jobs only registered recruiting agents may charge, with the Emigration Act, 1983 and the eMigrate portal fixing the maximum. Pay for training and we will place you is a known fraud. Chain schemes that pay you for recruiting members are banned under the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978, and unregulated deposit-taking is an offence under the BUDS Act, 2019. A moneylender must be registered under the state moneylending Act, and courts can reopen extortionate interest under the Usurious Loans Act, 1918.
tips.benefit: The Code on Wages, 2019 limits deductions to permitted categories and provides a claims route. The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and state Shops Acts add record-keeping duties. The Emigration Act, 1983 requires recruiting agents for overseas work to be registered, with service charges capped and complaints handled through eMigrate and the Protector of Emigrants. The Prize Chits Act, 1978 bans money-circulation schemes, and the BUDS Act, 2019 criminalises unregulated deposit schemes. RBI digital lending rules require a key facts statement with the all-in annual percentage rate before disbursal.
tips.sources: Code on Wages, 2019. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Emigration Act, 1983 and eMigrate. <https://emigrate.gov.in/>; Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; RBI digital lending guidelines. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: India has no single statute that says no recruitment fee for every job; the protection is a patchwork of the Code on Wages, state Shops Acts, the Emigration Act for overseas work, and general cheating law. There is also no four-times-LPR interest cap: the Usurious Loans Act lets a court reopen an unconscionable rate, and state moneylending Acts set their own ceilings. Do not hand over originals even to an HR department for verification: show them and take them back the same day.

tips.title: Public rental housing in India means PMAY-U's affordable rental blocks - apply early, and do not expect a five-year guarantee
tips.cost: No fee to apply on the PMAY-U portal. You need Aadhaar, income proof and, for the affordable rental route, proof that you are a migrant or fall in the EWS or LIG band. The wait is the cost.
tips.inPlainWords: India's public housing push has been ownership-first, through Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. The rental arm is the Affordable Rental Housing Complexes scheme, which converts existing government-funded vacant housing and supports new dormitory or family units for urban migrants and the poor, run by urban local bodies and private partners. Some states and cities run their own rental housing, and housing boards rent a small number of units. There is no national waiting list with a five-year statutory guarantee. Applying is free, and earlier applications are considered first in most city queues.
tips.benefit: PMAY-U covers the EWS, LIG and MIG income bands, and the affordable rental route is aimed at migrants working in cities, industrial workers and labourers near construction sites. Units are allotted by the urban local body or the implementing partner on terms it publishes, usually with a rent below market and a licence period rather than a tenancy. State housing boards such as DDA in Delhi and MHADA in Maharashtra also run lotteries for rental and ownership stock. Applying does not commit you to anything.
tips.sources: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban. <https://pmaymis.gov.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs - Affordable Rental Housing Complexes. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Delhi Development Authority. <https://dda.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This is not a statutory entitlement with a maximum waiting period. ARHC units are limited, located where the implementing body has stock, and allocated on its own rules; some are dormitory beds, not family flats. Rental housing lotteries are heavily oversubscribed. Beware of agents selling PMAY application forms: the application is free and online.

tips.title: Food and rent are more than half of an Indian household's spending - a shared room and a kitchen are the two biggest levers
tips.cost: Finding a shared room takes a few days and usually one month's rent as deposit, plus brokerage if you use an agent. Cooking needs a stove, a cylinder or an induction plate, and about 45 minutes a day.
tips.inPlainWords: The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey for 2022-23 puts food at about 46 per cent of rural and 39 per cent of urban monthly spending, with rent and fuel taking most of the rest. Those two lines are where a tight budget is won or lost. A monthly shared room or PG bed is far cheaper per night than a lodge or a daily rental, and a kitchen shared with two or three people beats restaurant food within a week. If a job offers staff accommodation or a canteen, treat that as part of the salary. State-run subsidised canteens, such as Amma Canteens in Tamil Nadu and Indira Canteens in Karnataka, serve meals well below market price.
tips.benefit: The HCES 2022-23 figures show food at roughly 46 per cent of rural and 39 per cent of urban monthly consumption expenditure, with rent, fuel and light taking a large share of the rest; that is why these two categories respond best to a cut. A PG or shared flat spreads rent and electricity across several people, and a monthly rent contract is cheaper per night than a lodge. Cooking at home cuts the per-meal cost sharply once you have a stove and a cylinder. Employer-provided accommodation and canteen facilities are common in construction, security, hospitality and factory work, so ask before you accept the wage.
tips.sources: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation - Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2022-23. <https://mospi.gov.in/>; Department of Food and Public Distribution. <https://dfpd.gov.in/>; Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation - Amma Canteens. <https://www.tncsc.tn.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The percentage shares are national averages and differ sharply between states and between a single migrant and a family. There is no official data on how much a shared room saves; that part is practical judgment, not a statistic. Subsidised canteens are run by state governments and municipal bodies, and eligibility and timings vary. A PG deposit and brokerage can eat the first month's saving, so negotiate the deposit in writing.

tips.title: A gap in EPF or ESIC does not wipe your record - but the ten-year pension rule and ESIC's cover do have edges
tips.cost: No cost. Keep your UAN and your ESIC insurance number, and check the passbook and contribution history online. Do not pay an agent to keep your PF active.
tips.inPlainWords: Your EPF account does not lapse. It stays linked to your UAN, keeps earning interest, and can be transferred to a new employer or withdrawn. Pension is different: the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 needs ten years of pensionable service for a monthly pension, and below that you get a withdrawal benefit instead. ESIC cover runs with insurable employment: once you stop being an employee of a covered establishment and stop contributing, benefits end, though contribution conditions can keep some claims alive for a period. Employment injury benefit now sits in Chapter VII of the Social Security Code, 2020, which replaced the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923. PM-JAY has no contribution at all, so it cannot lapse. A gap damages schemes that demand continuous contribution, not your accumulated years.
tips.benefit: EPFO links every job through the UAN, so service across employers adds up and a transfer is online. Ten years of pensionable service gives a monthly EPS pension; nine years and eleven months gives a lump-sum withdrawal benefit. ESIC's cash benefits depend on contribution conditions, so a gap can cost you a claim even while you are still insured. PM-JAY eligibility is by household category, not contribution, so it survives unemployment. Checking your passbook once a year catches an employer who deducted but did not deposit.
tips.sources: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; Social Security Code, 2020, and the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 for contributions already paid; ESIC benefit conditions. <https://esic.gov.in/>; National Health Authority - PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/PM-JAY>
tips.caveats: There is no Indian rule that fifteen years of contribution earns a pension; the EPS threshold is ten years, and the amount depends on pensionable salary and service. ESIC benefit conditions are technical and change by circular, so check before you assume a gap is harmless. Paying a third party to run contributions in your name is a fraud risk and can void a claim. Withdrawing PF at every job change destroys the compounding that makes it worth anything.

tips.title: A criminal record, a default or a credit blacklist is not the end - but India has no individual bankruptcy law in force
tips.cost: Court fees are low and legal aid is free for eligible categories. The costs are time, travel and the conditions attached to any settlement. Your credit report is free once a year from each bureau.
tips.inPlainWords: Three different problems, three different routes. A criminal record: adult convictions are not sealed in India, and you must disclose them where the law or the form asks; records of a child in conflict with the law are destroyed under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 after the statutory period and cannot disqualify the child. A default: there is no operational personal bankruptcy in India, because the individual insolvency chapter of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 has never been brought into force, so the routes are a settlement with the lender, a Lok Adalat compromise, or a state debt relief Act for small debts. A credit blacklist: your record with CIBIL or another bureau is corrected by the lender, not by a credit repair agency, and you can dispute it and then complain to the RBI Ombudsman.
tips.benefit: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 requires records of a child in conflict with law to be destroyed after the prescribed period and bars any disqualification on that basis. For debt, a one-time settlement with the bank, a Lok Adalat award under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, or relief under a state debt relief Act, several of which exist for small and agricultural debtors, are the realistic routes. Credit information is governed by the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005: you can demand your free report, dispute an error with the lender, and escalate free of charge to the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021. A wilful-defaulter listing can be challenged before the bank's review committee and, later, a court.
tips.sources: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, section 24. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, Part III. <https://www.ibbi.gov.in/>; Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not expect an Indian equivalent of a personal bankruptcy discharge: the IBC's individual insolvency provisions are dormant, and the fresh start process has never been notified. State debt relief Acts cover only small debts and are patchy. Paying a credit repair firm cannot remove a genuine default, and only the lender can correct an error. Disclosure duties for convictions depend on the job: government service, teaching and the bar have their own bars.

tips.title: If you buy private health cover, look for lifetime renewability and a short pre-existing waiting period - not a guaranteed renewal clause
tips.cost: A family floater for a young household typically runs to several thousand rupees a year, and a senior-citizen policy much more. The time cost is reading the waiting periods, the room-rent cap and the co-payment before you pay.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian health policies do not use the phrase guaranteed renewal. The equivalent is lifetime renewability, which IRDAI requires insurers to offer on indemnity products: the insurer cannot refuse to renew on grounds of age or claims history. Two other clauses matter more than the premium. The pre-existing disease waiting period, which is capped at 36 months, and the moratorium, after which the insurer cannot contest a claim except for proven fraud. Check the room-rent limit, the co-payment and the sub-limits, because those decide what you actually get. If you are eligible for PM-JAY, buy this only as a top-up.
tips.benefit: IRDAI's health insurance regulations require lifetime renewability for indemnity policies, so renewal is a right rather than a favour. The standard product Arogya Sanjeevani gives plain, comparable cover with uniform terms and a cap on room rent. IRDAI's 2024 rules require insurers to offer health cover to all ages and to state the moratorium period, after which claims cannot be rejected except for fraud. Section 45 of the Insurance Act, 1938 does the same job for life policies: it bars an insurer from repudiating a life policy after three years on the ground of misstatement, while the three-year moratorium for a health policy rests on the IRDAI rules, not on section 45. Cashless authorisation at a network hospital avoids paying first.
tips.sources: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India - health insurance regulations and standard products. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Insurance Act, 1938, section 45. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Health Authority - PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/PM-JAY>
tips.caveats: This tip keeps its B grade: the rules are official, but there is no Indian data on how much a top-up policy saves a household. Guaranteed renewal is not Indian regulatory language; lifetime renewability is, and it still allows the insurer to change the premium at renewal with IRDAI approval. Non-disclosure of a pre-existing condition can still void a claim within the moratorium. Two indemnity policies will not pay the same bill twice. If PM-JAY or ESIC covers you, the marginal value of a private policy is smaller than the agent will suggest.

tips.title: Airport and station waiting areas are not shelters - in India the rain basera is safer, and it is still not a right
tips.cost: Free at a station or airport only if you hold a valid ticket or boarding pass; otherwise you will be moved on. A rain basera bed is usually free. Food and a chargeable waiting room cost money.
tips.inPlainWords: Sleeping at a railway station or airport is a common stopgap and a bad one: access is controlled by ticket checks, police and security staff move people on, and theft is common. India has no statutory 24-hour venue right. The safer option is a municipal night shelter, a rain basera, run under the urban shelter programme or by an NGO, or a state destitute home. For women, a One Stop Centre or the 181 helpline can arrange short shelter; for children, 1098. Keep your bag against your body, refuse food and drink from strangers, and do not sleep near tracks, rivers or construction sites.
tips.benefit: Rain baseras provide a bed, water and a toilet at little or no cost, and many urban local bodies publish shelter lists. One Stop Centres give women temporary shelter, medical aid and legal help. Childline 1098 is a 24-hour response line for children on the street. A station waiting room, where one exists, needs a valid ticket and is patrolled, which is both its advantage and its limit.
tips.sources: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs - DAY-NULM shelter for the urban homeless. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development - One Stop Centres and 181. <https://wcd.nic.in/>; Indian Railways - retiring rooms and waiting rooms. <https://indianrailways.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no direct Indian equivalent of a legal 24-hour refuge, and no official data on the safety of station floors. Shelter capacity is small and many are seasonal. Security staff can and do clear stations at night, and arguing with them is not a strategy. If you have no money and no bed, call 112 and ask for the nearest shelter, or go to a government hospital emergency department if you are unwell.

tips.title: Work out who actually employed you before you file: contractor, principal employer and household work have different routes
tips.cost: No fee. Establish three facts: whether the workplace is a registered establishment, whether you were hired through a contractor, and whether the work was in a private home. The Shram Suvidha portal and the establishment's registration certificate answer the first two.
tips.inPlainWords: The route depends on the employment relationship. If you were hired through a contractor at a factory, construction site or office, Chapter XI of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 applies once the establishment employs 50 or more contract workers (section 45), and it then makes the principal employer pay your wages if the contractor does not (section 55(3)) and provide the welfare facilities (section 53). On a construction site, the state BOCW welfare board may add accident, pension and maternity benefits. An unregistered establishment is still covered by the state Shops and Establishments Act and by the labour commissioner inspection power. Domestic work in a private home is the exception: most labour statutes exclude it, so the route is a civil suit or the state domestic workers board, not a labour court.
tips.benefit: Chapter XI of the OSH Code, 2020 applies to establishments with 50 or more contract workers (section 45); if the contractor does not pay, section 55(3) makes the principal employer pay the wage or the unpaid balance and recover it from the contractor, and section 53 makes the principal employer provide the welfare facilities to contract labour. The BOCW welfare framework can provide accident, pension and maternity benefits to registered construction workers. The Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979 is folded into the OSH Code, 2020. Some states run domestic workers welfare boards; there is no national domestic workers statute.
tips.sources: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (Chapter XI, sections 45, 53 and 55). <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Building and Other Construction Workers welfare framework. <https://labour.gov.in/>; Shram Suvidha portal. <https://shramsuvidha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The principal employer liability is for wages and welfare facilities, not reinstatement, and enforcing it needs the contractor records, which you may not have. Chapter XI applies at 50 or more contract workers, so on a smaller site the Code's contract-labour protections may not apply and the claim runs against the contractor. Domestic workers remain outside most labour law, and a civil suit is slow. A written order, a site gate pass and a photo of the attendance register are worth more than an oral promise.

tips.title: If you cannot repay a credit card or personal loan, call the lender's own number and ask for restructuring - never pay a debt relief agency
tips.cost: Zero to negotiate. Prepare salary slips or proof of job loss, a hospital record if illness caused it, and a written budget. Expect several calls and a written offer. Never pay an upfront fee to a third party.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian banks are not obliged to offer you a five-year instalment plan, but most have a board-approved restructuring or one-time settlement policy, and RBI's fair-practices rules require them to deal with you fairly and to follow recovery-agent rules. Call the number on the card or in the app, say clearly that you cannot pay the full amount but want to settle, and ask for the policy in writing. Keep paying something if you can. Do not borrow from an app to pay a card. Do not pay a debt settlement or credit repair firm: it cannot change a genuine default, and it often takes a fee and leaves you worse off.
tips.benefit: RBI's recovery-agent rules restrict calls to between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m., require the agent to identify themselves, and bar harassment of relatives and colleagues; breaches go to the lender's grievance officer and then the RBI Ombudsman. Restructuring and one-time settlements are commercial decisions under the bank's board-approved policy, often with a longer tenor and sometimes a waiver of penal interest. Credit information is governed by the CICRA, 2005: the lender must correct an error, and you can escalate free of charge to the RBI Ombudsman. RBI's digital lending rules require a key facts statement with the all-in cost before disbursal, and a cooling-off period for digital loans.
tips.sources: RBI - responsible lending conduct and recovery agents. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; RBI - digital lending guidelines. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no Indian statutory right to a five-year repayment plan, and a bank may refuse and sue. A civil suit takes a year or more. Not paying is not a crime by itself, but moving assets or disappearing after borrowing can turn a civil default into a criminal case. Answer the lender's calls and keep your contact details current. If an agent threatens you, complain to the lender and the RBI Ombudsman, and call 112 if you are in danger.
